result.summary: The environment is a typical auto-oriented commercial corridor with continuous but narrow sidewalks directly adjacent to on-street parking. There are no marked pedestrian crossings or traffic calming measures visible, creating a long, unprotected stretch for anyone needing to cross the street. The lack of a buffer and the presence of parked vehicles limit visibility and physical protection for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crossings
hazards.description: There are no designated or marked crossing points for pedestrians across the wide roadway, forcing unsafe mid-block crossings.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the main roadway in the foreground and mid-ground

hazards.name: Visual obstructions from parked cars
hazards.description: Parallel parked cars along the curb block the line of sight between pedestrians on the sidewalk and approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the image along the curb line

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install marked crosswalks with high-visibility patterns to designate safe crossing points and alert drivers to pedestrian presence.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct curb extensions at potential crossing points to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Furniture Zone
interventions.description: Add a buffer zone with trees or street furniture to provide physical and psychological separation between pedestrians and moving traffic.

result.summary: The environment is highly hostile to pedestrians, characterized by a complete absence of sidewalks and marked crossings on a wide, multi-lane roadway. The street edge is dominated by open parking lots and commercial driveways, creating numerous uncontrolled conflict points between vehicles and any potential pedestrians.

hazards.name: Missing Sidewalks
hazards.description: There is no dedicated space for pedestrians on either side of the road, forcing anyone on foot to walk in the roadway or through active parking lots.
hazards.location_in_image: Both sides of the roadway throughout the frame

hazards.name: Excessive Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The wide multi-lane road lacks any marked crossings or refuge islands, making it dangerous for pedestrians to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the roadway

hazards.name: Uncontrolled Driveway Access
hazards.description: The lack of defined curbs or driveways means vehicles can enter or exit the adjacent parking lots at almost any point, creating unpredictable conflict zones.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image at the auto service entrance

interventions.title: Sidewalk Installation
interventions.description: Construct continuous paved sidewalks on both sides of the street to provide a safe, dedicated space for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Marked Crosswalks and Pedestrian Refuge
interventions.description: Install high-visibility marked crosswalks and a center refuge island to reduce the unprotected crossing distance.

interventions.title: Access Management
interventions.description: Install curbs and consolidate driveways to limit vehicle access points and reduce the number of conflict locations with pedestrians.

result.summary: The street environment features a continuous sidewalk on the right side but lacks a protected walkway on the left due to a large gas station apron. There are no marked crosswalks or traffic calming measures visible, and the wide, open roadway may encourage higher vehicle speeds.

hazards.name: Unmarked wide roadway
hazards.description: The lack of clear lane markings and the wide street width can lead to higher vehicle speeds and unpredictable driver behavior.
hazards.location_in_image: Center roadway

hazards.name: Gas station apron conflict zone
hazards.description: The large, undefined vehicle access area for the gas station creates a significant conflict zone where pedestrians have no protected space.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the image

hazards.name: Lack of pedestrian crossings
hazards.description: There are no marked crosswalks visible, forcing pedestrians to cross an open roadway without protection or priority.
hazards.location_in_image: Entire visible roadway

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install high-visibility crosswalks to provide designated and safer crossing points for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Add curb extensions at potential crossing points to reduce crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Driveway Management
interventions.description: Define the gas station entrance more clearly with a standard driveway cut to reduce the width of the conflict zone and maintain sidewalk continuity.

result.summary: The image depicts a commercial mid-block environment with a continuous, relatively wide concrete sidewalk. While the walkway is clear and fronted by active businesses, it lacks a physical buffer or green infrastructure to separate pedestrians from the adjacent parking and travel lanes.

hazards.name: Visual obstruction from parked cars
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the curb line can obstruct the sightlines between drivers and pedestrians, particularly if someone attempts to cross mid-block.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curb line in the foreground and background.

hazards.name: Lack of pedestrian-vehicle buffer
hazards.description: The sidewalk is directly adjacent to the parking lane with no physical separation such as a planting strip, furniture zone, or bollards.
hazards.location_in_image: The entire length of the sidewalk shown.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at the nearest intersections to improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians and to shorten the crossing distance.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Buffer Zone
interventions.description: Introduce a furniture or planting zone between the walkway and the curb to provide a physical and psychological buffer from traffic.
